Pixel-grid snapping: `--pixel-grid` turns generated "pixel art" into true one-pixel-per-cell sprites, in `convert`, generation and `batch`.

- **`--pixel-grid auto|SIZE`:** generated pixel art isn't on a true grid. Each art pixel is several image pixels wide, often a fractional size, the cells are unevenly placed and their edges are soft, so downscaling with `--resize --nearest` gives uneven pixels. `--pixel-grid` finds the real cell grid and writes one pixel per cell: the cell's dominant colour, with alpha fully solid or fully clear. Cell sizes in real generated sheets ranged from 4.7 to 19 px. See [Pixel art](https://github.com/foksa/codex-img#pixel-art) in the README.
- **`auto` or a size:** `auto` measures the edges along each axis, tries cell sizes from 4 px up to a sixteenth of the short side, fits the cell boundaries to the drawn edges and keeps the best fit. It's meant for images you know are pixel art: it refuses paintings, watercolours, photos and smooth renders (weak edge capture, impure cells, or fewer than 16 cells on the short side), but flat vector illustrations and JPEG block artefacts can still pass, so check the result. A size such as `8` or `7.5` (fractional sizes are fine) skips the search and never refuses for confidence; use it when `auto` refuses art you know is pixel art, or picks a multiple of the real cell size.
- **Pipeline order:** `--key` runs first, so a removed background becomes transparent cells. Then the snap, then `--palette`, which maps each cell to its nearest palette colour (no despeckle, so one-cell details stay; adding a palette doesn't change the grid), then `--trim` (on cells, so the `--json` `trim` rectangle is in cells) and `--resize`. For a crisp preview, add `--resize` with `--nearest` at a whole multiple of the snapped width; the palette colours stay exact.
- **Refusals:** in `convert`, a refusal is an error: exit code 1, nothing written, and the message names the measurements and suggests passing a size. When generating, in `batch` too, the image has already cost quota, so it is saved un-snapped with a warning instead of being lost. Generation keeps the untouched original as `<name>.raw.<ext>`, as with `--trim` and `--resize`. `rerun` and `refine` keep the setting.
- **`--json` `pixelGrid`:** `period` and `offset` per axis in image pixels, `mode` (`regular` or `elastic`), `cells` `[columns, rows]`, `capture`, `purity` and `coherence`. After a refusal it is `{refused: true, reasons, measurements}`, and `convert --json` prints it on the failed input's line with `input` and `error`.
- **Batch `pixel_grid`:** assets and defaults accept `pixel_grid: "auto"` or a cell size such as `8` or `7.5`, checked by `codex-img check` and the batch JSON schema.
- **Core API:** library users get `codex_img_core::pixel_grid`: `detect(&RgbaImage, &DetectOptions)` returns a `Grid` (periods, offsets, fractional cell boundaries, cell counts and the confidence measurements) or a `Refusal` with its reasons, and `snap(&RgbaImage, &Grid)` writes one pixel per cell. `transform::PixelGrid` (`Auto` or `Size`) runs it as part of a conversion.
